   STAFF REPORT

 Meeting Date:  March 24, 2025

 To:  Community Security Ad Hoc Liaisons Honorable Mayor Friedman
  & Councilmember Corman

 From:  Joana Torres, Community Services Manager

 Subject:  Safety and Hospitality Services

 Attachment:  None

INTRODUCTION
Staff has been working with the Community Security Ad Hoc Liaisons to select a service
provider and bring forward a recommendation for award of a new agreement for
Ambassador safety and hospitality services. At the February 21, 2025 Liaison meeting,
the Community Security Ad Hoc Liaisons recommended an extension of Block by Block’s
(BBB) current agreement, at the current rates and scope of service, until June 30, 2025.
That action was approved by the full City Council on March 4, 2025. This allows finalist
responders to the current Request for Proposals to provide additional information
requested by the Ad Hoc and to host follow-up interviews with those finalists, enabling the
Ad Hoc to conduct necessary research and deliberation for a thorough recommendation
to the City Council without the pressure of a looming contractual deadline or a lapse in
services.

DISCUSSION
At the September 30, 2024 Community Security Ad Hoc Liaison meeting, the Ad Hoc
proposed a new scope of work for Safety and Hospitality Services along with consolidation
of services, reduction of routes, and consolidation of shifts. This included consolidation of
overnight security functions and parking garage checks with current public safety
contractor, as they are more integrated with BHPD for security services and engaged
throughout the City.

There was also a recommendation to reduce the footprint for hospitality services.
Hospitality services in the Business Triangle and South Beverly Drive would maintain
current service levels, while reducing Ambassador coverage outside of these areas. Areas
with reduced Ambassador coverage, which generally do not have major hospitality
functions, such as the City Hall campus, are currently patrolled by current public safety
contractor, and will be consolidated. Lastly, the Ad Hoc recommended a reduction in the
hours of service and number of shifts provided by Ambassadors to better align with the
peak visitor hours.
 Meeting Date: March 24, 2025
A Request for Proposals was published on November 15, 2024 and closed on December
20, 2024. A total of seven proposals were received. Staff interviewed the top five
responders and recommended two finalists for referral to the Ad Hoc. The top two
responders met with the Community Security Ad Hoc Liaisons on February 4, 2025.

Following this meeting, the Ad Hoc met again on February 21, 2025 and requested
additional information from both responders before making their recommendation to the
full City Council, as well as the recommendation to extend BBB through June 30, 2025.
The follow up interviews will take place before the scheduled Community Security Ad Hoc
Liaison meeting on March 24, 2025.

FISCAL IMPACT
It is anticipated that award of any agreement would require an appropriation of funds, as
the full budgeted amount for these services will have been expended by the end of the
current agreement on June 30, 2025 and the annual pricing provided by both responders
is higher than what is currently budgeted for.

RECOMMENDATION
Staff will bring forward the Ad Hoc’s recommendation to the full City Council along with a
request to appropriate the funds needed to award the agreement.

  Stephanie Harris,
  Director of Community Services
  Approved By
